:- student(N1, S1, M1), student(N2, S2, M2), N1 != N2, M1 == M2.

% 1. Hattie and the student who will major in Theology are different students.
:- student("Hattie", _, "Theology").

% 2.1 The student who will major in English and Tracy are different.
:- student("Tracy", _, "English").

% 2.2 The student who will major in English is Tracy or the student who received the $25,000 scholarship.
% That is: if someone majors in English, then they are Tracy or they received $25,000.
:- student(N, S, "English"), N != "Tracy", S != 25000.

% 2.3 Tracy is Tracy or the student who received the $25,000 scholarship.
% This is logically always true (since "Tracy is Tracy" is true), so it imposes no constraint.
% Therefore, we can ignore it.

% 3. Hattie was awarded $10,000 more than the person who will major in Physics.
% So: Hattie's scholarship = Physics major's scholarship + 10000.
:- student("Hattie", S1, _), student(_, S2, "Physics"), S1 != S2 + 10000.

% 4. The student who received the $40,000 scholarship will major in Theology.
:- student(_, S, M), S == 40000, M != "Theology".

% 5. Ora was awarded some amount less than the student who will major in Archaeology.
% So: Ora's scholarship < Archaeology major's scholarship.
:- student("Ora", S1, _), student(_, S2, "Archaeology"), S1 >= S2.
